summary:
I resumed from the earlier run's rebuild 2 (pose v10). It already passed every gate but left three one-pixel see-through holes in the mask: (923,612), (962,647) and (961,648), which produced the 50.3 px contour max. An exact ray check through the builder's own field (/tmp/calib-right/seethru.py) reproduced those three pixels exactly. They come from two places: the tip of the V between the middle and ring fingers, and a small gap where the ring, little finger and thumb meet. Changes in this run, all confirmed with Blender rebuilds 3-7:
(1) Middle finger: middle_pip r 24->23, middle_dip r 21->20. The DIP moved (854,610)->(854,608) (the 606 of rebuild 3, set back to 608 in rebuild 5 to keep the middle tip on the reference tip). The render's underside had sat 5-9 px below the particle outline at x 875-905.
(2) Thumb: thumb_mcp r 29->27 and moved 3 px up to (1032,670); thumb_ip r 27.5->27 so the radius tapers. The bottom outline at x 1000-1060 had been 7-10 px low.
(3) Little finger: pinky_dip r 19->17 (proper taper, narrower tip). pinky_mcp r 24->26 closes the ring/little/thumb gap.
(4) Ring: ring_mcp (972,596)->(978,598). The knuckles now form a plausible arc (the ring MCP was 3.5 mm beyond the middle MCP along the hand axis, now 1 mm), and it sits 6 px nearer its reference reading.
(5) Palm: flat 0.35->0.30, which shrinks the oversized palm slab in 3D (at 70 % wrist->knuckles, 110x44 mm -> 104x39 mm) for +0.03 px contour mean.
Depth is the earlier run's reconstruction, which I re-derived and kept:
- For a RIGHT hand pointing left with the index on top (D1), the palm must face the camera. Because the ring and little finger curl 125-155 px DOWN in the image, the palm also faces substantially downward. So the back of the hand faces up and away: dorsal (0.459, 0.669, -0.585). D12's reading of the top outline as the back of the index finger agrees.
- The knuckle line recedes from the index (z 0.13) to the little finger (z -0.115).
- The thumb (z 0.24-0.30) lies in front of the palm and of the ring and little fingers, whose middle phalanges pass behind it.
- The middle, ring and little fingers flex toward the camera. Their depths are solved from anatomical 3D bone lengths.
- The index lies in the image plane at the left index tip's depth (0.13), so the fingertips nearly touch in 3D.
Only ring_mcp is within 0.01 of the left pose in both z and flat (1 of 23 joints, a coincidence).
Final result: IoU 0.931, contour mean 3.34 / p95 7.62 px, negative space 0.879, tips 1.0/1.4/2.2/4.2 px, all 16 joints within 3u, no mask holes. A1 and D9 pass.

anatomy:
Scale: 2.3 px/mm, taken from the index, which lies in the image plane. Bone lengths are given as projected px / 3D px (3D mm). "Before" is the pose at the start of step 2 (commit 1b6b85d = /tmp/calib-right/pose-right.orig.json); "after" is the final pose.
THUMB. CMC-MCP 80.9/93.6 (40.7) -> 115.3/113.5 (49.3). MCP-IP 74.5/73.9 (32.1) -> 75.4/72.4 (31.5). IP-tip 55.0/52.4 (22.8) -> 60.3/56.8 (24.7).
INDEX. 96.6/93.5 (40.7) -> 104.8/102.2 (44.4). 60.5/58.9 (25.6) -> 58.2/56.7 (24.7). 66.7/65.2 (28.3) -> 46.8/45.6 (19.8). Before, the distal segment was longer than the middle phalanx; that is fixed.
MIDDLE. 93.4/92.5 (40.2) -> 79.6/103.5 (45.0). 59.7/59.5 (25.9) -> 53.5/62.1 (27.0). 55.9/56.0 (24.3) -> 64.4/61.2 (26.6).
RING. 85.1/86.3 (37.5) -> 77.1/96.6 (42.0). 61.1/61.9 (26.9) -> 56.0/59.8 (26.0). 45.5/46.2 (20.1) -> 48.1/48.3 (21.0).
LITTLE. 57.0/59.3 (25.8) -> 54.8/75.9 (33.0). 44.0/45.4 (19.7) -> 46.3/46.3 (20.1). 32.1/33.1 (14.4) -> 25.0/43.7 (19.0).
Finger totals after: middle 98.6 mm > ring 89.0 = index 88.9 > little 72 mm, the anatomical order. The middle's distal segment is about as long as its middle phalanx (its projection is already longer than the 22 mm target).
RADII r, base to tip, before -> after:
- thumb 32/25/22/18 -> 32/27/27/19
- index 21/18/15.5/11.5 -> 30/24.5/20.5/12.5
- middle 21/19/16/12 -> 28/23/20/13.5
- ring 20/18/16/12 -> 28/25/22/13
- little 18/16/15/12 -> 26/19/17/12.5
Every chain is non-increasing, and the fingers are 20-45 % fuller, as the particle outline is. The builder's 3D half-widths (px) fall along each chain: index 32.2->14.1, middle 31.7->16.3, ring 32.5->16.1, little 31.1->15.8, thumb 28.7->21.2. The ring is about 10 % wider than the middle at the PIP, following the reference's wide ring below the thumb (45-48 px).
KNUCKLES. MCP spacing 25.9/22.3/21.7 mm (index to little finger 68 mm). Distance along the hand axis from the wrist: index 137.7, middle 138.9, ring 139.9, little 133.0 mm. That is a plausible arc; the ring was 3.5 mm beyond the middle before this run's ring MCP move.
NO DIGIT PASSES THROUGH ANOTHER (/tmp/calib-right/clearance.py, finger roots excluded). The closest surfaces are the ring and little proximal phalanges at -2.8 px (about 1 mm of side-by-side contact, conservative estimate) and middle/ring at -0.5 px. All other pairs are at least 10 px apart. The thumb is 36 px clear of the ring's distal phalanx and in front of it.
PALM AND WRIST. Wrist to MCPs is about 138 mm at the finger scale, against about 90-95 mm in a real hand. The reference hand is long between its wrist narrowing (1282,710; wrist keypoint 0.5 px) and the knuckles. The left pose shows the same trait: wrist-to-middle-MCP over middle finger length is 1.64 on the left and 1.42 on the right. Palm sections in 3D: at 50 % wrist->knuckles 115 x 59 mm (including the thenar), at 70 % 104 x 39 mm, at 85 % 90 x 26 mm. That is broader and thicker than anatomical (see openIssues).
DEPTH READING (not copied: 1 of 23 joints within 0.01 of the left pose in both z and flat).
- D1 (index on top) plus right-hand chirality means the palm faces the camera. The ring and little finger curl downward, which also turns the palm down. So dorsal points up and away, and D12's "back of the index finger" agrees.
- The radial side (index, thumb) is nearest; the knuckle line recedes to the little finger.
- The thumb is in front of the palm and of the ring and little fingers.
- The flexed middle, ring and little fingers come toward the camera: z of middle PIP/DIP/tip 0.18/0.25/0.25; ring 0.08/0.14/0.17; little 0.00/0.00/0.08. These are solved from the 3D bone lengths.
- The index is flat at z 0.13, the left index tip's depth.
DIGIT IDENTITY (D1), checked in right-view-home.png at 4x:
- INDEX is the top digit, reaching to (807,438); its silhouette tip is (807,437).
- MIDDLE is the long digit pointing left beneath it; tip (816,660), silhouette tip (811,653).
- THUMB is the short digit ending at (897,672); the GLB tip is 0.42 px from it at z 0.30. Its nail relief faces up and toward the camera and is the only nail visible in the home view: the finger nails face away because the back of the hand does (final-home-thumb-4x.png).
- RING (905,754) and LITTLE (993,752) curl down.
VIEWS (final rebuild 7, --views; midway look at rebuild 4). home, yawp35, yawm35 and above are all volumetric, with no paper-thin cut-out; the phalanges are rounded, with knuckles. The palm reads as a broad slab with a crisp radial edge in yawm35 and above. The known off-frame forearm cuff shows in yawm35 and above (step 3).
meshReport:
Final build is rebuild 7, and it is on disk: outputs/qa/calib/right-mesh-report.json.
A1: 1 shell, 0 non-manifold edges, 0 boundary edges. The welded GLB read-back also shows 0 boundary / 0 non-manifold / 0 unwelded boundary. Winding agreement 100 % (GLB 1.0). 28 854 triangles and 14 429 vertices (limit 30k).
D9 contour coverage: 100 % / 100 % (4-/8-connected boundary), largest uncovered run 0 px, 0 inner polylines on background. PASS; outer polylines have mean precision 0.52 px.
Every rebuild in this run (3-7) kept identical A1 numbers. A notes-only rebuild (6) reproduced the GLB byte-identically and the mask pixel-identically.
Report caveat: fingertips.thumb reports delta 90.3 px. This is an artifact of the report, present since rebuild 2: its search cylinder has no end, so it picks up the middle fingertip further along the thumb's axis. Measured on the GLB with the search capped just past the tip (/tmp/calib-right/glbtips.py), the thumb tip is 0.42 px from the pose. The other tips are 0.51-1.52 px.
openIssues: Palm too broad and thick in 3D (all gates still pass). Field cross-sections of the final mesh, at the 2.3 px/mm finger scale: 115 x 59 mm at 50 % wrist->knuckles (including the thenar), 104 x 39 mm at 70 %; an anatomical palm is about 80-85 x 30 mm. Cause: a single carpus capsule (palm r 102) has to fill a palm silhouette about 190 px tall while the palm is turned about 54 deg from the camera, which the downward curl of the ring and little finger requires. Slimming it from the pose fails the gates (preview: palm r 90 gives mean 3.81 / p95 11.2; r 80 gives IoU 0.897). flat 0.35->0.30 was taken at no cost; 0.25 would add +0.6 px p95. It shows as a boxy slab with a crisp radial edge in right-view-yawm35.png and right-view-above.png (crops /tmp/calib-right/r3/v7-yawm35-2x.png, v7-above-2x.png). See builderRequests.

Reference-data observation for the main session (no gate or reference file touched): right-mask.png has a small dent right at the tail cut, (1322-1335, 683-707), just outside right-ignore.png. Its 32 edge pixels lie 17-33 px from any render edge, because a forearm that leaves the frame cannot follow the dent. It accounts for the contour max 33.1 px and about 0.13 px of the contour mean (3.34 -> 3.21 without it). Evidence: /tmp/calib-right/r3/tailcut-ignore-5x.png.

Local residuals within tolerance, all visible in /tmp/calib-right/r3/final-fingers-2x.png, final-ring-pinky-4x.png and final-palm-wrist-2x.png:
- Wrist-top particle bump at (1230-1255, 599-624), 15-18 px; a smooth forearm cannot carry it.
- The ring finger's left edge sits 5-7 px inside the reference at y 640-690.
- Middle/ring pocket: the render's V reaches (925,610) where the reference's rounded pocket ends near x 912. Moving ring_pip left fixes both of the above but reopens a 1-11 px see-through hole at (958-961, 645-648) between ring, little finger and thumb (tested with seethru.py), so it was not taken.
- The index PIP dorsal knuckle bump rises 4-6 px above the reference's straight (D12) back of the finger at x 900-920.
- The index tip's upper side is up to 7 px fuller than the pointed particle tip; the tip itself is 1 px off.
The index-tip contact gap needs both hands, so the main session checks it. The right index silhouette tip is (807,437), 1 px from the reference; index_tip z 0.13 equals the left pose's.
ring_mcp is the one joint within 0.01 of the left pose in both z and flat (z -0.045 vs -0.05, flat 0.85 both): a coincidence of the knuckle-line reconstruction. The other 22 joints and dorsal differ.

The thumb's nail relief is subtle (nail_relief 0.12). In the particle image the thumbnail outline is the thumb's most legible feature (D1). Whether the particle sampler shows it is a step 3/5 question.
builderRequests: Palm form (step 3): let the palm silhouette be filled with anatomical volumes instead of one oversized carpus capsule. Options: offset the carpus section toward the palmar side, or build the palm from a thinner metacarpal plate plus thenar/hypothenar masses. Today a projected palm height of about 190 px forces a slab of about 115 x 59 mm (at 50 % wrist->knuckles) with a crisp radial edge. Evidence: /tmp/calib-right/palmsec.py numbers in openIssues, right-view-yawm35.png, right-view-above.png.

Mesh report fingertip check: cap the search along the distal axis (for example along < 1.3 x the distal segment) or restrict it to the digit's own vertices. For the right thumb it now reports mesh_tip_px (810.9,644.9), delta 90.3 px, which is the middle fingertip; the capped measurement is 0.42 px (/tmp/calib-right/glbtips.py).
Forearm cuff at the off-frame arm extension (already scheduled for step 3); visible in right-view-yawm35.png and right-view-above.png.

Optional: the dorsal IP knuckle bumps (ip_knuckle_size / ip_knuckle_lift) put a 4-6 px bump on the right index's top silhouette at the PIP, where D12 reads the back of the finger as straight. A per-hand or smaller setting would let the pose follow the reference.

Optional: make the right thumb's nail relief more legible for the particle sampler (nail_relief is 0.12 of the tip thickness); the reference shows the thumbnail outline as the thumb's defining feature (D1).
